title: Electromagnetic Spectrum for Wireless Communication
markdown:
Wireless communication uses a portion of the **electromagnetic (EM) spectrum** — the full range of frequencies at which electromagnetic energy can propagate.

{{viz:0}}

### Bands Used for Networking

The wireless spectrum relevant to data communication is divided into three major regions:

| Region | Frequency Range | Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| **Radio waves & Microwaves** | 3 kHz – 300 GHz | The widest usable band. Covers everything from AM radio to satellite links and cellular networks. |
| **Infrared** | 300 GHz – 400 THz | Short-range, line-of-sight. Used by remote controls, IrDA ports, and some indoor wireless links. |
| **Visible light** | 400 THz – 900 THz | A very narrow band. Emerging technologies (Li-Fi) use it for high-speed indoor communication. |

> **Note**: Higher frequencies generally provide more bandwidth (higher data rates) but suffer from shorter range and greater atmospheric absorption.
